items.text: The staging step reads from an external system, the same SQL Server connection used for HQ analytics already found for another cross reference table, pulling from the vendor and store lists there. This confirms that two other tables' source data, previously unlocated in the current database, does live behind that same external connection, which makes it more likely, though still not proven, that those two tables' own update processes use the same connection

This table is kept up to date by a fully confirmed daily process. A first step stages fresh data, clearing and reloading it every run, and a second step combines it with the store location and vendor lists, matching all 86,005 of the table's current rows

A second, older process for updating this table is confirmed inactive. It read from a staging table that has been frozen since 2016, and a note in its calling process confirms it was deliberately shut down in August 2016. A related file that fed the same staging table used by the still-active process carries no author-set schedule at all, the same signature already seen elsewhere in this project for inactive processes; its own calling process carries the identical shutdown note. Both calling files carry an internal warning that part of them is disconnected and does not run as written, so this confirms these specific steps, not that everything else in those files runs end to end

The inactive process contains a leftover notification message that incorrectly refers to a different table, left over from being copied from another table's setup. This is only leftover text, not evidence the process actually updates the wrong table; its real target is confirmed correctly elsewhere in the same file
No invalid vendor or location keys and no duplicate vendor-location pairs were found, and every row carries the approved status

blocks.text: Still open, not confirmed in code or data yet. None of this blocks the lineage above, it is tracked here so nothing gets forgotten.

items.text: It is plausible, but not directly confirmed, that the main vendor table and the adjustment code table are also fed by the same external HQ analytics connection confirmed here
items.note: If the same connection serves all of them, that is one migration source to replace instead of several separate unresolved ones; worth confirming directly with the Weis team rather than inferring further from shared table names alone
